ideas.title: SSL certificate, domain expiry & DNS change monitor
ideas.problem: Expired certs and lapsed domains take sites and email down; renewal automation fails silently

evidence.note: TrackSSL: SSL cert monitoring, $5,276 MRR, 221 active subs, $195k all-time (TrustMRR, Oct 2026)
Kit.domains: domain expiry/SSL/DNS monitor, $118 MRR, 4 subs
UptimeObserver: uptime/SSL/DNS monitor, $130 MRR, 22 subs
DNS Monit: DNS/SPF/DKIM/DMARC monitor, $137 all-time, lifetime deal

ideas.notes: Proven by TrackSSL. Monitors only public certs/DNS of domains the user adds (passive, like a browser). Liability: a missed alert is a silent failure, so you need redundant checks, alert-delivery tests, and ToS liability caps. Agency multi-client dashboard is the wedge.

ideas.title: SPF/DKIM/DMARC checker + plain-English DMARC report monitor
ideas.problem: Gmail/Yahoo bulk-sender rules made DMARC mandatory-ish; SMB owners can't read XML aggregate reports or fix SPF lookups

evidence.note: Dmarclytics: solo DMARC/SPF/DKIM monitor, $100/mo
DMARCLY: $157.1k annual revenue (Apr 2021) before acquisition
DNS Monit: DNS/SPF/DKIM/DMARC monitor, $137 all-time, lifetime deal
OutboundQA: email infra pre-flight ($49 one-time / $79/mo), no active subs, listed for sale

ideas.notes: DNS lookups are public. DMARC reports contain sender IPs and metadata only, so state retention in the privacy policy. Crowded, and indie results are mixed (Dmarclytics $100/mo, DNS Monit $137 all-time). Win with a single fix-it wizard per sender (Xero, Mailchimp, M365).

ideas.title: Essential Eight Maturity Level 1 self-assessment & evidence tracker (AU SMB)
ideas.problem: SMBs are told to 'do the Essential Eight' but the ASD material is written for IT staff
ideas.monetisation: Free assessment + one-time report or subscription

evidence.note: EssentialScore: free 74-question E8 self-assessment, $99 one-time policies + gap report
CyberSmart360: E8 compliance SaaS $49/mo founding, $89/mo from Nov 2026
ASD Annual Cyber Threat Report 2024-25: avg self-reported small-business cybercrime cost $56,600 (+14%); 84,700+ reports
ACSC small business cyber security guide (MFA, updates, backups first)

ideas.notes: Never call it certification or compliance. It's a self-assessment with an 'as reported by you' disclaimer. Avoid storing evidence files (screenshots can hold credentials). The market already has 4+ AU entrants, so the edge would be distribution through accountants.

ideas.title: Cyber insurance application prep pack (MFA, backups, admin evidence)
ideas.problem: Proposal forms ask yes/no questions (MFA everywhere? tested backups?); a wrong 'yes' risks a denied claim

evidence.note: AU SME cyber insurance applications ask about MFA, backups, admin accounts
DUAL AU cyber proposal form
ASD Annual Cyber Threat Report 2024-25: avg self-reported small-business cybercrime cost $56,600 (+14%); 84,700+ reports

ideas.notes: The tool must never fill in the insurer's form or tell the user an answer. It explains what each question means and lists the evidence to collect. Duty of disclosure stays with the insured, so carry a strong disclaimer. Brokers are the distribution channel.

ideas.title: Local read-only Google Workspace / M365 security config audit
ideas.problem: Small orgs never check MFA enforcement, admin count, mail forwarding rules or external sharing
ideas.monetisation: One-time per tenant or MSP subscription

evidence.note: ArgusSec: free OSS Google Workspace audit (227 checks), EUR 15/mo hosted
Snoka: free local read-only Google Workspace scanner
FailSafe: M365/Workspace posture from $49/mo

ideas.notes: Run it locally so admin tokens and findings never leave the device. That reduces breach and NDB exposure, because no hosted copy of the org's config exists. Use read-only scopes only. Google admin directory scopes need verification. Free OSS competitors are strong.

ideas.title: Staff offboarding & quarterly access-review checklist across SaaS
ideas.problem: When staff leave, shared passwords and SaaS accounts linger; nobody reviews who has access

evidence.note: ACSC small business cyber security guide (MFA, updates, backups first)
ASD Annual Cyber Threat Report 2024-25: avg self-reported small-business cybercrime cost $56,600 (+14%); 84,700+ reports

ideas.notes: Advisory checklist plus a manual app inventory, with optional read-only user lists from Google/M365. It stores no credentials and makes no automated deprovisioning (avoids fail-silently liability). Recurring reminders give natural retention.

ideas.title: 2-minute monthly phishing-awareness lessons for small teams
ideas.problem: SMB staff click BEC and invoice-fraud emails; enterprise training is overkill

evidence.note: ASD Annual Cyber Threat Report 2024-25: avg self-reported small-business cybercrime cost $56,600 (+14%); 84,700+ reports
ACSC small business cyber security guide (MFA, updates, backups first)

ideas.notes: Education only: no simulated phishing sends (spoofing creates deliverability, consent and ToS problems). Heavily saturated, so it's a feature of the offboarding/E8 product rather than a standalone idea.

ideas.title: Security questionnaire answer bank & export for tiny SaaS
ideas.problem: Indie SaaS founders lose deals to 200-row spreadsheets asking about encryption, backups, MFA

evidence.note: SecurityQ: security questionnaire answering tool
QuestShield: questionnaire tool for startups
ComplyJet questionnaire automation (bundled compliance)
TrustMRR security category: 190 startups with verified revenue; Comp AI (SOC 2/ISO) $736k last 30d; Cloud Backup for Podio $2.4k MRR

ideas.notes: User-authored answers library. Optional AI drafting is BYOK and always marked 'review before sending'. Liability: a false answer becomes a contractual misrepresentation by the user, so the tool never invents controls. Good synergy with your indie-dev audience.

ideas.title: Trust/security page + security.txt + privacy policy starter for indie apps
ideas.problem: Indie apps need a privacy policy, security.txt and data-handling page to pass buyer and store review

evidence.note: OAIC: most businesses at or under A$3m turnover exempt from Privacy Act, with exceptions

ideas.notes: Feeder for the portfolio. Templates are not legal advice; generate from the user's own answers only. Good SEO.

ideas.title: Owner-verified security check for vibe-coded apps (exposed keys, Supabase RLS, headers)
ideas.problem: AI-built apps ship with leaked API keys in bundles, open Supabase tables and missing headers
ideas.target_users: Vibe coders, indie hackers, no-code builders

evidence.note: CheckVibe: scanner for AI-built apps, $807 MRR, 32 subs, $12,205 all-time (Oct 2026)

ideas.notes: Hard rule: scan only after domain ownership is proven (DNS TXT or file) or a connected repo. Unauthorised testing of others' systems risks Criminal Code Part 10.7. Never claim 'secure': report findings with a 'not a pen test' disclaimer. CheckVibe shows demand ($12k all-time) and also competition.

ideas.title: Security headers & CSP builder/checker
ideas.problem: CSP is hard to write; headers are misconfigured
ideas.notes: Passive fetch of public headers only. A free SEO feeder for the developer security cluster.

ideas.title: GitHub Actions workflow hardener (pin SHAs, least-privilege permissions)
ideas.problem: Supply-chain attacks via unpinned actions (tj-actions); default token permissions too broad

evidence.note: StepSecurity Harden-Runner: free for public repos; private repos need Enterprise
tj-actions/changed-files compromise: pin actions to commit SHA

ideas.notes: Read-only analysis plus suggested PRs the user merges. It never auto-pushes. Well served by free tools, so it fits as a feeder/upsell to the vibe-app scanner.

ideas.title: Local secret scanner & .env hygiene menu-bar app
ideas.problem: Devs commit keys; .env files sprawl across projects
ideas.notes: Runs locally and never uploads. Free CLIs dominate, so it's a feeder unless bundled with the dev disk reclaimer or dev-env-diff.

ideas.title: Dependency licence + vulnerability handover report for agencies
ideas.problem: Agencies must hand clients a licence and vuln summary; tools are enterprise-priced
ideas.notes: Licence 'compliance' wording is legal-adjacent: present facts (SPDX ids), not legal conclusions. Low defensibility.

ideas.title: Mac login items & launch agents auditor (signed? who made it? when added?)
ideas.problem: Macs accumulate background agents from uninstalled apps; users can't tell what's legit
ideas.target_users: Mac users, IT helpers, family tech support

evidence.note: LoginToggle: $9 one-time login items/launch agents manager
AgentView: $11.99 one-time LaunchAgents/cron inspector
Lingon Pro: $23.99 one-time launchd editor
Objective-See: free open-source Mac security tools (LuLu, KnockKnock, BlockBlock), nonprofit + Patreon

ideas.notes: Read-only by default. Disabling needs a confirm plus undo, and never deletes. Don't claim 'malware detection', which makes it a security product with a silent-failure risk. Present it as 'what runs on your Mac'. Fits the Mac shell. Free Objective-See tools cap the price.

ideas.title: Mac privacy permissions auditor (camera, mic, screen recording, full disk, accessibility)
ideas.problem: Users forget which apps were granted screen recording or accessibility; System Settings is scattered

evidence.note: Objective-See: free open-source Mac security tools (LuLu, KnockKnock, BlockBlock), nonprofit + Patreon

ideas.notes: Reading the TCC database needs Full Disk Access and an undocumented format that changes with each macOS release (maintenance and platform risk). Read-only; it links to the right Settings pane.

ideas.title: Lightweight per-app network connection viewer (no firewall)
ideas.problem: Users want to see what apps phone home without a full firewall

evidence.note: Little Snitch: $59 licence, 20+ years, Mac network monitor
Objective Development GmbH (Little Snitch, LaunchBar): 2025 profit EUR 492.5k, about 7 staff
Objective-See: free open-source Mac security tools (LuLu, KnockKnock, BlockBlock), nonprofit + Patreon

ideas.notes: Little Snitch proves a 20-year business (Objective Development: 2025 profit EUR 492.5k), but it's entrenched and LuLu is free. Network Extension entitlement adds build risk. Viewer-only keeps the liability low.

ideas.title: Auto-redact secrets & personal info in screenshots before sharing (local OCR)
ideas.problem: People paste screenshots with API keys, emails, card digits or addresses into Slack, Reddit and support tickets
ideas.notes: Local OCR (Vision framework), so no upload. Silent-failure risk (missed redaction), so always show a preview with 'review before sharing' and never claim completeness. Strong fit with the Mac shell and the local-first theme.

ideas.title: Clipboard secret guard (auto-clear copied keys/passwords, warn on paste)
ideas.problem: Secrets linger in clipboard history managers and get pasted into the wrong window
ideas.notes: Feeder. Pattern-based detection stays local.

ideas.title: Drag-drop file encryption for sharing (recipient decrypts in browser, locally)
ideas.problem: Sending tax returns, IDs and contracts by email in the clear; zip passwords are weak
ideas.notes: Crypto must use vetted libraries (age/libsodium), never home-rolled, and you need an independent review before launch. A bug fails silently with catastrophic results. You hold no keys or files, so there's no custody.

ideas.title: Account recovery planner (where each recovery method and backup code lives, never the codes)
ideas.problem: People get locked out of Apple, Google, myGov or email after losing a phone; recovery info is scattered
ideas.target_users: Everyone, especially families and older users

evidence.note: Quietkeep: $14.99 one-time offline digital legacy planner
Digital legacy tools comparison 2026 (crowded)

ideas.notes: Records locations and instructions only, never passwords or codes, so a leak isn't catastrophic. Local-first with printable output. Pairs with the legacy planner.

ideas.title: Digital legacy organiser & executor instructions
ideas.problem: Families can't find or close a deceased person's accounts, subscriptions or photos

evidence.note: Quietkeep: $14.99 one-time offline digital legacy planner
Digital legacy tools comparison 2026 (crowded)

ideas.notes: Not a will and not legal advice: link to state succession info. Very crowded. Stores no credentials.

ideas.title: Personal 2FA/passkey coverage checkup (guided, nothing stored server-side)
ideas.problem: People don't know which accounts lack 2FA or passkeys
ideas.notes: Feeder for the recovery planner. Never asks for credentials. Account-setting links change often.

ideas.title: Local password export auditor (reuse, weak, pwned via k-anonymity)
ideas.problem: Users without a manager don't know their reused/pwned passwords

evidence.note: HIBP API: Core from $4.39/mo; Pwned Passwords free (k-anonymity)

ideas.notes: Avoid. It handles plaintext password exports, so any leak or telemetry bug is a disaster, and platforms already do this for free. Recorded so future runs skip it.

ideas.title: Family breach-exposure dashboard via HIBP API
ideas.problem: Families want one place to see which members' emails appeared in breaches

evidence.note: HIBP API: Core from $4.39/mo; Pwned Passwords free (k-anonymity)
HIBP ToS: no third-party/reseller use unless plan permits; no building a similar breach search service

ideas.notes: HIBP ToS restricts third-party/reseller use and bans building a similar breach search service. You also have to verify each email's owner. Free alternatives are everywhere, so the platform risk is high.

ideas.title: DIY data-broker opt-out tracker (templates + re-listing reminders)
ideas.problem: Paid removal services cost US$100+/yr; DIY takes many hours and brokers relist

evidence.note: Delisted: free, donation-funded data-broker removal by one founder

ideas.notes: The user sends every request themselves and the tool holds no identity documents, which keeps liability low. Broker forms change constantly (maintenance). Mostly a US market, so it's a weak fit with the AU home market.

ideas.title: Done-for-you data-broker removal as authorised agent
ideas.problem: Same as DIY, but users want it fully handled

evidence.note: Delisted: free, donation-funded data-broker removal by one founder

ideas.notes: Avoid for a solo builder: you hold identity documents and act legally as an agent (CCPA authorised-agent rules), it needs ops-heavy maintenance, and VC-funded players dominate.

ideas.title: Suspicious text/email explainer (red flags + where to report; never says 'safe')
ideas.problem: Scam texts are convincing; older relatives forward them asking 'is this real?'

evidence.note: NASC Targeting Scams 2025: 29,058 text-scam reports, $17.98m lost via SMS

ideas.notes: Liability: a 'safe' verdict on a scam invites reliance claims. Show only red flags plus 'verify via the official number', and link to Scamwatch reporting. Process locally or BYOK and keep no message logs. Feeder with high AU search volume.

ideas.title: Home tech security checkup for parents/grandparents (printable)
ideas.problem: Adult children do ad-hoc tech support; no checklist for router, updates, backups, scams

evidence.note: ACSC small business cyber security guide (MFA, updates, backups first)

ideas.notes: Advisory checklist only. Good feeder bundle with the recovery planner.

ideas.title: Creator account takeover prevention kit (YouTube/Instagram/TikTok)
ideas.problem: Channel hijacks via fake sponsorship malware and session theft; recovery is slow
ideas.notes: Checklist plus team access review. Stores no credentials. Underserved, with a clear audience on creator forums.

ideas.title: One-page incident response plan + links to official NDB & ransomware-reporting guidance (AU SMB)
ideas.problem: SMBs freeze during an incident and don't know who to call or what must be reported

evidence.note: Cyber Security Act 2024: ransomware payment report within 72h for businesses with turnover of A$3m or more (from 30 May 2025)
OAIC NDB scheme guidance
OAIC: most businesses at or under A$3m turnover exempt from Privacy Act, with exceptions

ideas.notes: Legal score 2: deciding whether an NDB notification or a 72-hour ransomware report is required is legal advice. The tool may only link to the OAIC/ASD official guidance and can't make the decision. Keep it as a contacts/roles runbook.

ideas.title: Backup restore-test reminder & log (Essential Eight 'tested backups')
ideas.problem: Everyone has backups; nobody tests restores until it's too late

evidence.note: ACSC small business cyber security guide (MFA, updates, backups first)
EssentialScore: free 74-question E8 self-assessment, $99 one-time policies + gap report

ideas.notes: A log of human-performed tests, so it makes no claim that backups work. Low build/maintenance effort, but weak distribution on its own; best as part of the E8 tracker.

ideas.title: Dangling DNS / subdomain takeover check for your own domains
ideas.problem: Old CNAMEs to deleted Heroku/S3/Vercel apps can be taken over

evidence.note: DNS Monit: DNS/SPF/DKIM/DMARC monitor, $137 all-time, lifetime deal

ideas.notes: Verified domains only. Better as a feature of the SSL/DNS monitor than as a standalone product.

ideas.title: Personal-information register & APP-aligned privacy policy builder (AU SMB)
ideas.problem: AU Privacy Act changes (Dec 2026 transparency rules) and NDB duties confuse SMBs that aren't exempt
ideas.target_users: AU SMBs over A$3m turnover, health providers

evidence.note: OAIC: most businesses at or under A$3m turnover exempt from Privacy Act, with exceptions
Privacy Act changes from 10 Dec 2026 for SMBs; small-business exemption removal not yet law
OAIC NDB scheme guidance

ideas.notes: Template plus inventory only, not legal advice. The proposed removal of the small-business exemption would expand the market if it passes, so re-check each run.

ideas.title: Camera/mic usage log & alert for Mac
ideas.problem: Users want a history of which app used the camera/mic

evidence.note: Objective-See: free open-source Mac security tools (LuLu, KnockKnock, BlockBlock), nonprofit + Patreon

ideas.notes: Feeder: free OverSight and the built-in indicator cap willingness to pay.

ideas.title: QR code & short-link previewer (true destination before opening)
ideas.problem: Quishing: QR codes on parking meters and letters lead to phishing sites

evidence.note: NASC Targeting Scams 2025: 29,058 text-scam reports, $17.98m lost via SMS

ideas.notes: Shows the destination only, never a 'safe' verdict. Feeder.

ideas.title: Scan any website for vulnerabilities (no ownership check)
ideas.problem: Users want to scan sites they don't own
ideas.notes: Killed: unauthorised scanning of third-party systems (Criminal Code Part 10.7), dual-use, and host ToS.

ideas.title: Email/phone OSINT people lookup
ideas.problem: Find accounts and info linked to a person
ideas.notes: Killed: privacy harm, stalking/doxxing risk, Privacy Act and APP collection issues, and scraping against ToS.

ideas.title: Build-your-own password manager / credential vault
ideas.problem: Users want a simpler password manager
ideas.notes: Killed: credential custody. A breach is catastrophic, there's NDB exposure, and you'd be up against free platform managers.

ideas.title: Parental monitoring / device tracking app
ideas.problem: Parents want to monitor kids' devices
ideas.notes: Killed: children's data, stalkerware risk, and app store policy.

evidence.note: Cloud Backup for Podio: scheduled backup of one SaaS via API, $2.4k MRR (TrustMRR security category)

ideas.notes: Template idea: repeat per target. Use official APIs/OAuth only; never scrape against ToS. Aim to get listed as the vendor's integration partner. R2: recurring 3->4, because 'scheduled backup' framing (a security angle) supports subscriptions, per Cloud Backup for Podio.
